title: How gas particles make pressure inside a balloon
examples: Why does a balloon stay blown up?
Why does a balloon burst in the sun?

explain.say: Blow up a balloon and tie it. Nothing seems to move inside, yet something keeps it round and tight. What is holding it up? Billions of tiny air particles, all zooming about. Let us zoom in.

draw.text: How gas particles make pressure inside a balloon

explain.say: Look at the dots on the board. Each one is a gas particle, flying fast in a straight line until it hits something. In air they are far apart, with lots of empty space between them. Can you see any two dots stuck together?

No, they bounce right off! Every time a particle hits the balloon wall, it gives a tiny push. Billions of pushes every second, spread over the wall, make gas pressure. Pressure means force on each square metre. That push keeps the balloon round.

Now let us heat the gas. Look at this graph. As the temperature goes up, the particles move faster and hit harder and more often. So the pressure rises in a straight line. What might happen to a balloon left in hot sun?

marks.label: Hot: harder hits
marks.ask: Why does heating a gas raise its pressure?

explain.say: It could swell and even pop, well reasoned! That is why tyre pressure is checked when tyres are cool. Wow fact: each breath of air holds about ten thousand billion billion particles. Challenge: squash a balloon gently. Why does it push back harder?

marks.label: Hot: harder hits
marks.ask: Why does heating a gas raise its pressure?

faq.a: Gas particles move fast and keep hitting the walls of their container. All those tiny pushes added together make the pressure.
asks: Why do gases push on their container?

faq.q: Why does heating a gas raise its pressure?
faq.a: Heat makes the particles move faster, so they hit the walls harder and more often, which increases the pressure.
asks: Why do tyres have higher pressure when hot?

faq.q: Why does squashing a gas raise its pressure?
faq.a: In a smaller space the particles hit the walls more often, so the pressure goes up.
asks: Why does a squeezed balloon push back?

faq.q: Why are gases easy to squash?
faq.a: Gas particles are far apart with lots of empty space between them, so you can push them closer together.
asks: Why can you compress a gas?

faq.q: Why does a balloon stay blown up?
faq.a: The air particles inside push outwards on the rubber just as hard as the stretched rubber and the outside air push in.

facts: Gas pressure is caused by particles colliding with the walls of their container.
At constant volume, a gas's pressure rises as its temperature rises.

quiz.say: What makes the pressure inside a balloon?
quiz.show: What makes the pressure inside a balloon?
quiz.why: Billions of particle collisions with the wall each second create the outward push.

wrong.0: Gas particles bounce off; they do not stick.
wrong.1: The rubber is light; the push comes from moving air particles.

quiz.say: A sealed can of gas is heated. What happens to the pressure?
quiz.show: A sealed can of gas is heated. What happens to the pressure?
quiz.why: Hotter particles move faster and hit the walls harder and more often.

wrong.1: Faster particles hit harder, so the pressure cannot fall.
wrong.2: Temperature changes particle speed, so the pressure changes.
